answer.rationale: With p99 already 5x target on the write path during peak settlement traffic, every minute costs writes. The prior consolidation (memory_b1) confirms that rolling back a release cleared a checkout error spike on a stable prior build with no customer impact, and memory_b4 shows circuit breakers contained a partner outage by failing fast. A rollback is the single fastest path to recover write-path latency without dropping customer writes, and it doesn't require new capacity, a failover, or a traffic rebalance — each of which would be a second intervention I'd have to defer. I'll keep the rollback small and guarded, stop at the first sign the regression doesn't reverse on the prior build, and hold the circuit-breaker option in reserve as the next-window action if rollback doesn't recover latency.
